evals.prompt: What is the reviewbot unhappy about on CL 481203?
evals.expected_output: audit mode, scoped to the bot by the request: collapsed bot findings with per-finding state (live/stale/wrong/blocked), proposed fixes, human comments counted and named as scoped out, written to gerrit-review-fix-plan.md. No edits, no push.

evals.prompt: Address the review comments on my current change.
evals.expected_output: full mode: resolves change from local Change-Id trailer, verifies HEAD match, classifies every author as bot or human, reports both sets in chat with no plan file, stops at Phase 5 and asks which fixes to apply and which replies to post.

evals.prompt: Apply the approved fixes in ./gerrit-review-fix-plan.md and push the patchset.
evals.expected_output: fix mode: re-reads comments, re-checks approved findings against current code and flags stale ones, drops replies whose threads closed, applies fixes, runs repo checks, amends preserving Change-Id, asks before pushing to refs/for, then stages replies as drafts and publishes once.

evals.prompt: The bot flagged a hardcoded password in config.ts on CL 481210 — clear it and push.
evals.expected_output: Stops the fix flow on the secret finding. Explains that deleting the line leaves the secret in history and that rotation comes first. Does not push silently.

evals.prompt: The lint bot is wrong about the null deref on line 44 of other.ts in CL 481203 — tell it so.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the claim in Phase 3, marks it wrong, drafts an /aino naming the guard on line 41, asks for approval, then posts with in_reply_to set to the bot comment id. Does not post without approval.

evals.prompt: I pushed a new patchset 20 minutes ago, what does reviewbot say now?
evals.expected_output: Detects that the highest bot comment patchset is behind the current patchset and reports "not reviewed yet" rather than "clean". Offers the /aireview trigger. Does not wait, poll, or quote a turnaround time.

evals.prompt: Priya left a pile of comments on 35206 and gave me a -1. Sort it out.
evals.expected_output: full mode on the human set: reads the label votes to name Priya as blocking, rebuilds threads and acts on the last message in each, separates nits from blocking findings, fixes blocking correctness first, and drafts a reply for every thread including the ones needing no edit. Stops for approval before editing or posting.

evals.prompt: Sam says the retry loop in poller.go doesn't back off, but I already fixed that two patchsets ago. Close it out.
evals.expected_output: Marks the finding stale after checking the current code, makes no edit, and drafts a reply naming the patchset that fixed it rather than an /aino. Does not resolve Sam's thread on his behalf, and does not use /aino on a human comment.

evals.prompt: My reviewer on 35206 thinks the map deref on line 44 can be nil but the guard on 38 covers it. Push back for me.
evals.expected_output: Grounds the claim, marks it wrong, and drafts a reply that cites line 38 and hands the decision back to the reviewer — not an /aino, not a resolved thread, and no second round of argument. Asks before posting.

evals.prompt: One of the reviewers wants me to split the config refactor out of 35206 into its own CL. Just do it.
evals.expected_output: Marks it blocked rather than attempting the split: the skill never rebases or reorders commits, and reverting hunks would leave a broken intermediate state. Reports the cost, drafts a reply offering the follow-up change, and hands the decision to the owner.

evals.prompt: There are 6 unresolved threads on my change from two reviewers plus the bot. Reply to all of them.
evals.expected_output: Drafts each reply at Phase 4, shows the full set of exact texts and asks once for the batch, stages them with post_draft_comment carrying in_reply_to, then calls publish_drafts a single time so the reviewers get one notification instead of six. Bot false positives go out as /aino in the same batch.
